***__Key Points__**​​

__
 
• ​The pronouns that connect a clause or phrase to a noun or a pronoun, is called a relative pronoun.
 
• The most common relative pronouns are:
 
 
• who, whom, whose, which, that.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *We don’t know the person who donated this money.*
 
• *You need to tick the box which says yes.​*
 
 
 
• ​We use 'who/whose' in relative clauses to refer to people, and sometimes to pet animals. (refer to the above example)
 
• We use 'which' in relative clauses to refer to animals and things, to introduce defining and non-defining relative clauses.
 
• We use 'whom' if the noun/pronoun is the object of the verb in the dependent clause.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The uncle whom we met at the family reunion is coming to visit. *(The noun 'uncle' is the object of the verb met.)
 
• *The person with whom I spoke was able to help me. *(The noun 'person' is the object of the preposition with.)
 
 
 
• ​Since we are referring to **'**one of the ways' in this sentence, 'which' will be used in the **blank **part of the sentence.

__
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in blank number 1 is option 3:** "species".**
 
• The term **"species"** is used in biological taxonomy and is the basic unit of classification.
 
• **It refers** to a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.
 
• **In this context,** it correctly refers to different types of rats that have been identified and classified. The Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) is an American partnership of federal agencies designed to provide consistent and reliable information on the taxonomy of biological species.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'According to the Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) there are more than 60 **species** of rat, which means they come in all sizes. They are (2) ________ 5 inches (12 centimeters), or longer, according to Encyclopedia Britannica. The largest species is the Bosavi woolly rat, which was (3)______ in 2009 in the rainforest of Papua New Guinea (and doesn't have a scientific name yet). It is (4)_____ the size of a cat - 32.2 inches (82 cm) from nose to tail and (5)______ around 3.3 lbs. (1.5 kilograms), according to CNN.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"Entities" **- this is a very broad term that can refer to anything that exists, whether it be a physical object, a concept, or a fact. It is too vague to be used in the specific biological context of different types of rats.
 
• **"Sections" -** this term is more typically used to refer to parts of a physical object or divisions within an organization or piece of writing. It's not used to refer to types of living organisms.
 
• **"Objects" **- this term usually refers to inanimate physical things, not living organisms.

subject: ENG
question: Areas like the southern part of Gujarat, eastern Tamil Nadu, northeast peninsula covering Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and East Madhya Pradesh receive rainfall between _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**100-200 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rainfall between 100-200 **cm is **received **in the **southern parts of Gujarat**, **east Tamil Nadu**, **northeastern Peninsula covering Odisha**, **Jharkhand**, **Bihar**, **eastern Madhya Pradesh**, **northern Ganga **plain along the **sub-Himalayas **and the **Cachar Valley **and **Manipur**.
 
• They are the **area of Medium Rainfall**.
 
• **Duration of the monsoon in India**-
 
 
• The **Southern part of India**, being **near to the sea**, **gets rainfall early **and **for a longer duration **than the **northern part**.
 
• **As rain-bearing winds cross western ghats **humidity **decreases **and so **does rainfall in the northern part of India**.
 
• The **Southern part **of India **receives rainfall from the southwest monsoon **and the retreating **southwest monsoon **(**northeast monsoon**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The monsoon rainfall **has a **declining **trend with **increasing distance **from the **sea**. **Kolkata receives 119 cm **during **the southwest monsoon period, Patna 105 cm**, **Allahabad 76 cm**, and **Delhi 56 cm**.
 
• The **highest rainfall **occurs along **the west coast**, on **the Western Ghats**, as well as in the **sub-Himalayan areas **in the **northeast **and the **hills of Meghalaya**. Here the **rainfall exceeds 200 cm**. In **some parts **of **Khasi and Jaintia hills**, the **rainfall exceeds 1,000 cm**. They are the **area of high Rainfall**.
 
• **Western Uttar Pradesh**, **Delhi**, **Haryana**, **Punjab**, **Jammu **and **Kashmir**, **eastern Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, and **Deccan Plateau **receives **rainfall between 50-100 cm**. They are the **area of Low Rainfall**.
 
• **Parts of the Peninsula**, especially in **Andhra Pradesh**, **Karnataka and Maharashtra**, **Ladakh**, and **most of western Rajasthan receive rainfall below 50 cm**. It is the **area of Inadequate Rainfall**.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A major ________ of modern times is that we have come to assume that all creation is ________ to the material interests of us, the homo-sapiens inhabiting earth, which has cut the _________ relationship we otherwise enjoyed with other constituents of creation
solution:
The correct answer is "**fallacy, subservient, symbiotic**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fallacy **means **untrue notions**.

 
 
• **Example**: *The belief that the corner house is haunted is a** fallacy.** *
 
 
 
• **Subservient** means **acting as subordinate**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Even though Willy is talented, he acts as a ****subservient*.** 
 
 
 
• **Symbiotic** means **dependence on each other equally**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Tina and her friend share a **symbiotic** relationship. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, the appropriate answer is "fallacy, subservient, symbiotic". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frankness** - being honest and open.
 
• **Superior** - in a higher rank or position.
 
• **Disadvantageous **- without any benefit. 
 
• **Accuracy** - exactly to the point. 
 
• **Domineering** - wanting to control other people with a strong character.
 
• **Encumbering** - a burden.
 
• **Felicity** - state of being very happy.
 
• **Disobedient** - refusal to listen to the rules.
 
• **Hindering** - troubling.

question:

The app gets Larry's parents involved in the learning and improvement process, sending them advice about Larry's behaviours and progress, and recommending motivational __________ they might undertake that are _________ to Larry's situation and the program's __________ about his attitudes and behaviours.
solution:
The correct answer is '**interventions, targeted, inferences**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** options to fill in the blanks are '**interventions, targeted, inferences**'.
 
• The word '**interventions**' means '**interference by a state in another's affairs**'.
 
• The word '**targeted**' means '**select as an object of attention or attack**'.
 
• The word '**Interference**' means '**the action of interfering or the process of being interfered with**'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is '**interventions, targeted, inferences**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's understand the other options.
 
 
• **Option 1**:

 
 
• **Intermissions**- *a pause or break.*
 
• **Directed**- *control the operations of; manage or govern.*
 
• **Injunctions**- *a judicial order restraining a person from beginning or continuing an action threatening or invading the legal right of another, or compelling a person to carry out a certain act.*
 
 
 
• **Option 2**: 
 
 
• **Interpolations**- *the insertion of something of a different nature into something else.*
 
• **Disrupted**- *drastically alter or destroy the structure of.*
 
• **Inventions**- *the action of inventing something, typically a process or device.*
 
 
 
• **Option 4**:
 
 
• **Interruptions**- *the action of interrupting or being interrupted.*
 
• **Disillusioned**- *disappointed in someone or something that one discovers to be less good than one had believed.*
 
• **Invasions**- *an incursion by a large number of people or things into a place or sphere of activity.*

subject: ENG
question: What is the central contradiction discussed in the passage regarding digital surveillance?

options.text: The need for transparency vs. secrecy
The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy
The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations
The trade-off between national security and individual freedom

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the central contradiction:***

 
 
• The very first sentence of the passage identifies the core issue as a "clear contradiction between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty."
 
• The second paragraph reinforces this theme by stating, "The underlying conflict, then, is how to balance personal privacy against national security."
 
• The passage focuses entirely on how the desire to keep nations safe (through surveillance) directly threatens the civil freedoms and privacy of individuals.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **The trade-off between national security and individual freedom.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (The need for transparency vs. secrecy)**: Incorrect. While an "open legal regime" is proposed as part of a solution, the fundamental problem driving the passage is security versus liberty, not just transparency versus secrecy.
 
• **Option 2 (The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy)**: Incorrect. The passage specifically pinpoints the "demands of modern security" as the opposing force to privacy, rather than just general technological progress.
 
• **Option 3 (The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations)**: Incorrect. The passage is concerned with the liberties and privacy of *citizens*. Corporations are mentioned as entities that, alongside governments, are capable of exercising surveillance, not as the victims losing their rights.

question: What is the primary concern raised by the passage regarding the psychological effects of social media on teenagers?

options.text: Social media fosters stronger relationships in teens

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The passage explicitly questions whether these platforms are **"reengineering the brains of adolescents, essentially changing the way they think and feel about the world."** This highlights a fundamental shift in how teenagers process information and emotions.
 
 
 
• ***Impact on Attention and Rewards:***
 
 
• The text mentions that **"dopamine-reinforced cycles"** habituate the brain for instant rewards, which lowers the ability for **"focused, in-depth attention."** This supports the idea that social media is fundamentally altering cognitive patterns.
 
 
 
• ***Analysis of Other Options:***
 
 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the passage focuses on the psychological burden and negative outcomes like anxiety and depression, rather than "stronger relationships."
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage suggests social media may *harm* cognitive development by lowering the ability for delayed rewards and focus.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Social media alters the way teens think and feel about the world.**

subject: ENG
question: The phrase "allowing remote control, colour customisation, and adaptive brightness" functions as:
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase begins with **"allowing,"** which is a **present participle** (a verb ending in *-ing* that acts as an adjective).
 
• In this sentence, the phrase "allowing remote control..." modifies the noun phrase **"Smart lighting systems."** It provides additional information about what these systems do or what their characteristics are.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1 (Gerund phrase):** A gerund also ends in *-ing* but functions as a **noun** (e.g., "Allowing remote control is a great feature"). In the passage, it is describing a noun, not acting as one.
 
• **Option 3 (Infinitive phrase):** An infinitive phrase starts with "to" plus a verb (e.g., "to allow").
 
• **Option 4 (Absolute phrase):** An absolute phrase modifies the entire sentence and usually consists of a noun followed by a participle (e.g., "The technology allowing remote control, users felt empowered"). This phrase is specifically tied to the subject "Smart lighting systems."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, distinguishing between a Gerund and a Present Participle is a common trap. If the '-ing' word describes a noun (adjective function), it's a **Participle**. If it is the subject or object of a sentence (noun function), it's a **Gerund**.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Luminosity:** The quality of being bright or emitting light.
 
• **Incandescent:** Emitting light as a result of being heated.
 
• **Convergence:** The process of moving toward union or uniformity.
 
• **Contemporary:** Belonging to or occurring in the present.

question: What is the main message of the passage?

options.text: Doctors are the only essential workers in a hospital
Hospital employees enjoy easy working hours
Hospital employees need recognition and support
Working in a hospital is fun and relaxing

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **main message**, we look for the core argument or conclusion the author reaches after presenting all the facts.
 
• The passage describes the **hardships** (long hours, stress, emotional burden) and the **critical roles** played by all hospital staff, not just doctors.
 
• The final paragraph provides the "call to action" or the ultimate point: *"However, **proper recognition, mental health support, and fair working conditions are still essential** to ensure the well-being of those who care for others."*
 
• **Option 3** directly summarizes this need for acknowledgement and better support systems for these workers.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** This **contradicts** the text, which emphasizes that "every hospital employee plays a critical role" and that others' contributions often go "unnoticed."
 
• **Option 2:** This is the **opposite** of the truth; the text states their lives are marked by "long hours" and "entire shifts without rest."
 
• **Option 4:** The passage uses words like "high stress," "emotional strain," and "suffering," which are the opposite of **"fun and relaxing."**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, the "Main Message" is usually found in the **concluding sentences** of the passage. While the middle paragraphs provide evidence of the struggle, the end explains why that struggle matters and what needs to change.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Around the clock:** Day and night without stopping.
 
• **Recognition:** Appreciation or acclaim for an achievement or service.
 
• **Well-being:** The state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.
 
• **Unnoticed:** Not seen or noticed; disregarded.

question: What is the main idea of the passage?

__
 
• The **main idea** of a passage summarizes its entire scope, including the introduction, the conflict, and the conclusion.
 
• The passage begins by acknowledging the **beauty and health benefits** of silver (regulating temperature, blood circulation).
 
• It then introduces a **cautionary note** (conflict) regarding poor quality alloys, allergies, and physical strain from heavy pieces.
 
• The final paragraph provides a **balanced conclusion**: enjoy the beauty and minor benefits of silver, but prioritize **purity** and **moderation**. This matches perfectly with **Option 3**.
 
• Why other options are incorrect:

• **Option 2:** Gold is never mentioned or compared in the text; this is an **out-of-context** distractor.
 
• **Option 4:** The passage specifically warns *against* artificial alloys and low-quality silver, making this statement **factually incorrect** based on the text.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, the main idea of a "Pros and Cons" passage is almost always a **balanced statement**. Look for words like "but," "however," or "while" in the options to find the one that bridges both sides of the argument.*

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the passage, the word **"indispensable"** is used to describe International Organisations: **"IOs are indispensable for organising multilateral actions..."**
 
• The context emphasizes that despite challenges like veto powers and resource constraints, these organisations are **essential or absolutely necessary** for confronting complex emergencies and maintaining peace.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1 (Easily replaceable):** This is an **antonym**. The passage calls their role "irreplaceable" in the very first sentence.
 
• **Option 3 (Optional but useful):** This diminishes the weight of the word; "indispensable" implies that without them, the system would fail.
 
• **Option 4 (Unlikely to succeed):** This refers to a lack of effectiveness, whereas "indispensable" refers to the necessity of their existence and function.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *The prefix **'in-'** often acts as a negation. "Dispense" means to do without; "dispensable" means you can do without it. Therefore, **"indispensable"** means you **cannot** do without it.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

subject: ENG
question: In the sentence, “Their leadership is often characterized by a collaborative approach, emotional intelligence, and resilience,” the verb **“is characterized” **is in:
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Tense Analysis: Present Tense***

 
 
• The auxiliary (helping) verb used in the sentence is **"is"**, which indicates that the action is occurring in the present tense. If it were past tense, the helping verb would be "was."
 
 
 
• ***Voice Analysis: Passive Voice***
 
 
• In the passive voice, the subject of the sentence is the recipient of the action rather than the doer. Here, the subject **"Their leadership"** receives the action of being characterized.
 
• A passive voice construction requires a form of the "to be" verb paired with a past participle. The phrase **"is characterized"** follows this exact formula.
 
• Additionally, the use of the preposition **"by"** to introduce the actual agents of the action ("a collaborative approach, emotional intelligence, and resilience") is a classic indicator of a passive sentence.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **passive voice, present tense.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (active voice, present tense)**: Incorrect because the subject is receiving the action, not performing it. An active equivalent would be: "A collaborative approach characterizes their leadership."
 
• **Option 3 (active voice, past tense)**: Incorrect due to both voice (it is passive) and tense (it uses "is" instead of "was").
 
• **Option 4 (passive voice, past tense)**: Incorrect because the auxiliary verb "is" places the sentence in the present tense. The past passive equivalent would be "was characterized."

The central dilemma discussed is determining who is responsible for providing financial, logistical, and humanitarian support to those displaced by climate change.

question:
Identify the **voice** (active or passive) and the **tense** of the verb in the sentence:

"Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste."
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sentence:** "Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste."
 
• **Voice Identification:**
 
 
• The subject **"Many healthcare institutions"** performs the action **"follow"**.
 
• Since the subject is doing the action, the sentence is in the **Active Voice**.
 
 
 
• **Tense Identification:**
 
 
• The verb **"follow"** is in its base form used with a plural subject.
 
• This indicates the **Simple Present Tense**, which describes general truths or habitual actions.
 
 
 
• **Additional Clause Explanation:**
 
 
• The clause **"hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste"** is in the **passive voice**, but it is only a subordinate clause.
 
• The question focuses on the **main verb of the sentence**, which is **"follow"** (active voice, simple present).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Identification:** *Active voice, simple present.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Passive voice, simple past

 
 
• Incorrect because the verb **"follow"** is not in passive voice and not in past tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** Active voice, present perfect
 
 
• Incorrect because present perfect would require **"have followed"**, which is not used in the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** Passive voice, present continuous
 
 
• Incorrect because present continuous passive would be **"are being followed"**, which is not present in the sentence.

question:
Identify the** part of speech** of the word **"properly" **in the sentence:

"If not handled and disposed of properly, this waste can pose serious risks to human health and the environment."
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Adverb**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"properly"** modifies the verbs **"handled"** and **"disposed"** by explaining *how* the actions were performed, which is a characteristic of an adverb.
 
• **Adverbs often **answer the questions how, when, where, and to what extent. In this case, "properly" is answering "how" the waste should be handled and disposed of.
 
• The word **"properly"** ends in -ly, which is a common suffix for adverbs, although not all words ending in -ly are adverbs.
 
• **Adverbs can modify **verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, further specifying or qualifying the action or characteristic they are describing.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective: **An adjective modifies or describes a noun or pronoun. In the given sentence, "properly" does not describe a noun, so it is not an adjective.
 
• **Preposition: **A preposition shows the relationship between words (e.g., in, on, at). "Properly" does not function as a preposition here.
 
• **Pronoun: **A pronoun replaces a noun (e.g., he, she, it). "Properly" is not replacing a noun, so it is not a pronoun.

• **Option 2** is the word the author chose to convey this specific meaning within the context of domestic safety.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In Reading Comprehension, when two synonyms are provided (like threat and hazard), always look for the word that the author has contextualized with descriptive modifiers. The author uses "hazardous" to describe low voltage devices, but specifically uses "hidden threats" to describe the danger posed by neglected maintenance.*

• **Option 4: "Curiosity"** – This refers to a strong desire to know or learn something, which the passage identifies as a *cause* of risk, not the danger itself.

subject: ENG
question:
Identify the voice (active or passive) and tense of the verb phrase "are intended" in the sentence:

"These examinations, which demand years of rigorous preparation, are intended to select only the most capable candidates."
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3** i.e '**Passive voice, simple present**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase **"are intended"** is in the passive voice, which means the subject is receiving the action of the verb.
 
• **In the simple present tense,** the passive voice is formed by using the present tense of the verb "to be" (am, is, are) followed by the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this case, "are" is the present tense of the verb "to be", and "intended" is the past participle of the main verb "intend".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active voice:** In an active voice sentence, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb. "These examinations select..." is an example of the active voice. 
 
• **Present perfect:** The present perfect tense is formed with "have/has" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "have intended" or "has intended".
 
• **Past perfect:** The past perfect tense is formed with "had" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "had intended".

• **Contextual Application:** In the passage, the author uses this phrase to emphasize that the rising mortality among CAs is not just a minor issue but an **urgent demand** for systemic reforms and institutional accountability.

• **Incorrect Options:** "Gentle suggestion" (Option 1) and "quiet warning" (Option 4) lack the intensity and urgency required by the word "clarion." "Ambiguous statement" (Option 3) is the opposite of a clarion call, which must be unmistakably clear.
 
• **Tone of the Passage:** The author uses powerful adjectives such as **"alarming," "deleterious,"** and **"burgeoning"** to set a serious tone, making a "loud and clear demand" the most appropriate meaning.
 
• **Synonyms:** Other synonyms for a clarion call include an **ultimatum**, a **battle cry**, or an **urgent appeal**.

• In this sentence, the clause **"that varied greatly from region to region"** modifies the noun **"sarees, ghagras, and salwar suits"**.
 
• This makes it a clear example of a relative clause functioning as an adjective clause.

 __

question:
In the sentence:

"While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that working from the office remains more effective for several reasons."

What is the part of speech of the word "flexibility"?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4** i.e '**Noun**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"flexibility"** is a **noun** because it refers to a quality or a state of being, specifically the ability to be easily modified.
 
• In the sentence, "flexibility" acts as the **direct object** of the verb "offers," answering the question of what remote work provides.
 
• The suffix **"-ity"** is a common indicator of a noun in English (e.g., activity, purity, responsibility).
 
• Nouns typically follow verbs like "offer," "provide," or "give" when those verbs are used to describe features or benefits.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective: **The adjective form is **"flexible,"** which would be used to describe a noun (e.g., "a flexible schedule"). 
 
• **Adverb**: The adverb form is **"flexibly,"** which would modify a verb or adjective (e.g., "to work flexibly").
 
• **Verb:** While **"flex"** is a related verb, "flexibility" itself cannot express an action; it only names the quality.

The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Descriptive adjective**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"psychological"** is a **descriptive adjective** because it describes the nature or kind of the noun "impact."
 
• **Descriptive adjectives** (also known as qualitative adjectives) add a quality or characteristic to the noun they modify, answering the question "What kind?"
 
• In this context, it specifies that the impact is related to the mind or mental state, rather than being a physical or financial impact.
 
• The suffix **"-ical"** is a common ending for adjectives derived from nouns (e.g., biology to biological, psychology to psychological).

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demonstrative adjective:** These point out specific nouns (e.g., **this** factor, **that** impact, **these** reasons). 
 
• **Quantitative adjective**: These describe the quantity or "how much" of a noun (e.g., **some** impact, **much** factor).
 
• **Interrogative adjective:** These are used with nouns to ask questions (e.g., **Which** factor? **What** impact?).

__
 
• In the sentence, the subject **"many people"** is performing the action of the verb **"choose,"** which is the defining characteristic of the **Active voice**.
 
• The structure follows a standard **Subject + Verb + Object/Complement** pattern (People + choose + to suffer).
 
• The verb **"choose"** is in its base form, indicating that the focus is on the doer of the action rather than the action being done to the subject.
 
• Although the question asks for the "tense," the provided options refer to **Voice** (Active/Passive) and **Mood** (Imperative/Interrogative). Among these, Active voice is the only grammatically accurate description.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive voice: **In passive voice, the subject receives the action (e.g., "Suffering is chosen by many people"). This is not the case in the original sentence. 
 
• **Imperative voice:** This is a mood used for commands or requests (e.g., "Do not suffer in silence!").
 
• **Interrogative voice:** This refers to a sentence that asks a question (e.g., "Do many people choose to suffer in silence?").

question: Identify the tense of the verb "is described" in the first sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Passive Voice Structure.***

 
 
• The phrase **"is described"** follows the standard structure for the **Simple Present Passive**: [Subject] + [is/am/are] + [Past Participle of the verb].
 
• In this sentence ("Old age **is** often **described** as..."), the subject "Old age" is receiving the action of being described by others, rather than performing the action itself.
 
 
 
• ***Tense Identification.***
 
 
• The auxiliary verb **"is"** indicates the **Present** tense.
 
• The main verb **"described"** is in its past participle form (V3), which is required for all passive constructions.
 
 
 
• ***Contrast with Other Tenses.***
 
 
• **Present Continuous** would be: "is being described."
 
• **Present Perfect** would be: "has been described."
 
• **Simple Present (Active)** would be: "describes."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Passive voice is frequently used in formal or objective writing (like this passage) to focus on the **experience** or **topic** (Old age) rather than the specific person doing the describing.

subject: ENG
question:
Choose the option that correctly converts this sentence into passive voice:

"Younger generations should respect older individuals."

options.text: Older individuals are respected by younger generations.
Older individuals should be respected by younger generations.
Older individuals have been respected by younger generations.
Older individuals must respected by younger generations.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Passive Voice with Modal Verbs.***

 
 
• When a sentence contains a modal verb like **"should,"** the passive voice follows this specific structure:
 
• **[Object] + [Modal Verb] + [be] + [Past Participle (V3)] + [by Subject]**
 
 
 
• ***Step-by-Step Conversion.***
 
 
• **Active:** Younger generations (Subject) + should (Modal) + respect (Verb) + older individuals (Object).
 
• **Passive:** Older individuals (Object) + should + **be** + **respected** (V3) + by younger generations (Subject).
 
 
 
• ***Analysis of Other Options.***
 
 
• **Option 1**: Changes the mood from a recommendation ("should") to a general fact ("are").
 
• **Option 3**: Changes the tense to Present Perfect ("have been").
 
• **Option 4**: Grammatically incorrect because it lacks the auxiliary "be."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Modal verbs include **can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will,** and **would.** In the passive voice, every one of these follows the **"Modal + be + V3"** rule.
 
• For example: "He **can** solve it" becomes "It **can be** solved by him."

question: Which of the following sentences is written in the active voice?

options.text: Sleep disturbances are often caused by excessive mobile use.
Real-life conversations are being replaced by virtual interactions.
Experts suggest setting boundaries for mobile use.
Notifications are checked constantly by people of all ages.

solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To answer this question, let's break down each sentence to identify the voice (active or passive) used in each:**

__
 
• **1. Sleep disturbances are often caused by excessive mobile use.**

 
 
• This sentence focuses on the recipient of the action (sleep disturbances).
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__ because it uses the auxiliary verb "are" + the past participle "caused," and the doer (mobile use) follows the word "by."
 
 
 
• **2. Real-life conversations are being replaced by virtual interactions.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on what is happening to the conversations.
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__. It uses the continuous passive form "are being replaced."
 
 
 
• **3. Experts suggest setting boundaries for mobile use.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on the doer (Experts) performing the action (suggest).
 
• This sentence is in the active voice__. The subject "Experts" is performing the action directly, and there is no "be" verb combined with a past participle to indicate passivity.
 
 
 
• **4. Notifications are checked constantly by people of all ages.**
 __
 
• This sentence focuses on the object being acted upon (Notifications).
 
• This sentence is in the passive voice__. It follows the structure: Object + "are" + past participle "checked" + "by" + Subject.
 
 
 
• __So, out of the given sentences, options 1, 2, and 4 are written in the passive voice, while option 3 is written in the active voice__.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.**

subject: ENG
question: The clause "wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates" is:
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Defining an Adjective Clause.***

 
 
• An **Adjective Clause** (also known as a relative clause) is a dependent clause that modifies a noun or pronoun. It typically starts with relative pronouns like *who, which, that* or relative adverbs like *where, when, **wherein***.
 
• In the sentence: "These imposts embody the principle of progressive taxation, **wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates**...", the clause starting with "wherein" provides more information about the noun phrase **"progressive taxation."**
 
 
 
• ***The Role of "Wherein".***
 
 
• The word "wherein" acts as a relative adverb meaning "in which." Since it describes the specific nature of the "progressive taxation" mentioned just before it, it functions exactly like an adjective.
 
 
 
• ***Eliminating Other Options.***
 
 
• **Option 1**: It does not explain "why" (cause) the taxation exists; it describes what it is.
 
• **Option 3**: It does not act as a subject or object (Noun Clause); it is a modifier.
 
• **Option 4**: While "wherein" can feel related to "where," in this context, it isn't describing a physical location (place), but rather a conceptual principle.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tax terminology often uses formal relative adverbs like **wherein**, **whereby**, or **whereof** to connect legal principles to their specific applications. These almost always form **Adjective Clauses**.

question:
Identify the type of the following sentence from the passage:

"Each region contributes a unique weaving style: such as Chanderi, Pochampally Ikat, and Kanjeevaram, reflecting the stories, rituals, and environments of its people."
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Simple sentence***

 
 
• A **simple sentence** contains only one independent clause. An independent clause has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is "Each region" and the verb is "contributes." Even though the sentence is long and contains lists and phrases, it only has one main subject-verb pair forming a single independent clause.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Compound sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A compound sentence must have at least two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (like and, but, or) or a semicolon. There is no second independent clause here.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A complex sentence requires one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause. The phrase starting with "reflecting" is a **participle phrase**, not a clause, because it does not have its own subject and finite verb.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Compound-complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This type requires at least two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses. This sentence meets neither requirement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clause vs. Phrase**: It is easy to confuse long phrases with clauses. A clause must have a **finite verb** (a verb that shows tense). "Reflecting" is a present participle (non-finite), so it forms a phrase that modifies the noun "style," not a new clause.
 
• **The Role of Colons**: The colon in this sentence is used to introduce a list of examples. It does not separate two different clauses, so it doesn't change the sentence type.

question:
What is the tense used in the sentence below, and why is it appropriate?

"World Handloom Day, observed every year on 7th August."

options.text: Past Continuous - because the event is ongoing
Present Perfect - because it has just happened
Present Simple - because it states a general fact
Future Simple - because it refers to a yearly event

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: Present Simple - because it states a general fact***

 
 
• The **Present Simple** tense is the standard choice for expressing general truths, scientific facts, and scheduled or recurring events.
 
• The phrase "every year" is a frequency marker that signals a habitual or fixed schedule, making the Present Simple appropriate. Even though "observed" is a past participle here, it functions within a reduced relative clause (e.g., "which *is observed*"), which is inherently in the Present Simple.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Past Continuous***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Past Continuous (e.g., "was observing") describes an action that was ongoing at a specific time in the past. It does not fit a recurring yearly event.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Present Perfect***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Present Perfect (e.g., "has observed") links the past to the present or describes a recently completed action. It is not used for fixed annual calendar dates.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Future Simple***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While the event will happen again in the future, we use the Present Simple to talk about fixed timetables and recurring celebrations (e.g., "Christmas *is* on December 25th").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

subject: ENG
question: In the sentence" Digital platforms, when judiciously curated, can also serve as catalysts for mental growth " the phrase " When judiciously curated" functions as:
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: Adverbial clause of time***

 
 
• The phrase "when judiciously curated" is an **elliptical adverbial clause**. It is a shortened form of "when *they are* judiciously curated."
 
• It functions as an adverbial clause of time (or condition) because it specifies the specific circumstances or "time" under which digital platforms serve as catalysts for growth.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Noun clause***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A noun clause functions as a subject or an object (e.g., "I know *when the platforms are curated*"). In this sentence, the phrase is not acting as a noun.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Adjective clause***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. An adjective clause (relative clause) typically begins with a relative pronoun (which, that, who) and modifies a noun directly (e.g., "Digital platforms *that are curated*..."). While this phrase follows a noun, "when" establishes a relationship of time/condition to the action of the verb.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Absolute phrase***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. An absolute phrase modifies a whole sentence and usually consists of a noun followed by a participle, without a subordinating conjunction (e.g., "The *platforms having been curated*, the children began to play"). The presence of "when" makes it a clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellipsis in Clauses**: In English, we often omit the subject and the verb "to be" in adverbial clauses when the subject is the same as the subject in the main clause (Digital platforms).
 
• **Vocabulary**: "Judiciously" means with good judgment or sense. "Curated" means selected, organized, and looked after.
 
• **Context**: The author uses this clause to provide a necessary caveat—that digital platforms are only beneficial if they are chosen wisely.

question: Identify the tense in "can also serve as catalysts for mental growth".
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Simple present***

 
 
• The phrase "can also serve" uses the modal verb **"can"** followed by the base form of the verb **"serve."**
 
• In English grammar, modal verbs like can, may, must, and should are used in the **Simple Present** tense to express current ability, possibility, or general truths.
 
• The sentence describes a general fact or potential that exists in the present regarding digital platforms.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Present continuous***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The present continuous requires a form of "to be" + verb-ing (e.g., "are serving").
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Future simple***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The future simple typically uses "will" or "shall" + base verb (e.g., "will serve"). While "can" can imply future possibility, it is grammatically categorized as a present modal.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Present perfect***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The present perfect requires "has/have" + past participle (e.g., "have served").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modals and Tense**: Modal verbs do not change their form to show tense in the same way regular verbs do. "Can" is the present form, while "could" is often used as the past or conditional form.
 
• **Function of "Can"**: In this context, "can" indicates **possibility**. It suggests that digital platforms have the potential to act as catalysts, provided the conditions (like being "judiciously curated") are met.
 
• **Catalyst**: A term borrowed from chemistry, used here metaphorically to mean something that precipitates or accelerates an event or change (in this case, mental growth).

subject: ENG
question:
Identify the type of the following sentence and justify your answer:

"Improper disposal of e-waste allows these toxins to seep into soil and water bodies, causing severe environmental degradation and posing long-term health risks."
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Simple sentence***

 
 
• A **simple sentence** consists of only one independent clause. An independent clause contains a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.
 
• In this sentence, the subject is **"Improper disposal of e-waste"** and the main finite verb is **"allows."**
 
• Although the sentence is long, the phrases "causing severe environmental degradation" and "posing long-term health risks" are **participle phrases**. They do not have their own subjects and finite verbs, so they do not form separate clauses.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Compound sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A compound sentence must have at least two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so). This sentence only contains one independent clause.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A complex sentence requires one independent clause and at least one dependent (subordinate) clause (usually starting with words like because, although, which, who, that). There is no dependent clause here.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Compound-complex sentence***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This type requires at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finite vs. Non-finite Verbs**: In this sentence, **"allows"** is a finite verb (it shows tense). **"Causing"** and **"posing"** are non-finite verbs (present participles). A clause must have a finite verb; therefore, these participle phrases do not count as clauses.
 
• **Identifying Simple Sentences**: Do not be misled by sentence length. A sentence can be very long due to modifiers, lists, or prepositional phrases, but as long as it contains only one subject-verb pair forming a complete thought, it remains a simple sentence.
 
• **Context**: The passage uses this structure to clearly state the direct consequence of improper e-waste disposal on the environment and health.

subject: ENG
question:
Transform the above assertive sentence into an interrogative sentence.

"Electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life."

options.text: Why electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life?
Had electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life?
Are electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?
Have electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: Have electronic devices become indispensable to modern life?***

 
 
• To transform an **assertive** sentence into an **interrogative** (Yes/No) sentence, we move the auxiliary verb to the beginning of the sentence, before the subject.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** ("have become"). Therefore, we move the auxiliary **"Have"** to the front: *Have + Subject (electronic devices) + Verb (become)...?*
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Why electronic devices have become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While it is a question, it lacks the necessary subject-auxiliary inversion. A correct "wh-" question would be: "Why **have** electronic devices become...?"
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Had electronic devices have become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. It incorrectly changes the tense to Past Perfect ("Had") and includes a redundant auxiliary "have."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Are electronic devices become...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The auxiliary "are" belongs to the continuous or passive voice, but the main verb "become" requires the auxiliary "have" for the perfect tense used in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule for Transformation**: If the assertive sentence has an auxiliary verb (is, are, have, has, will, can), simply swap the position of the subject and the auxiliary.
 
• **Adding "Do/Does/Did"**: If the assertive sentence has no auxiliary verb (e.g., "They recycle e-waste"), use a form of "do" to create the question (e.g., "**Do** they recycle e-waste?").
 
• **Punctuation**: Always remember to replace the full stop (.) with a question mark (?) at the end of the sentence.

question:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate preposition:

International organisations worked together to launch initiatives aimed ___ increasing female literacy rates.
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4 (At)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: On***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “On increasing” is not idiomatic in this context; it would sound awkward and ungrammatical.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: For***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Aimed for increasing” is not standard usage. “For” works with nouns (“aimed for success”), but not with gerunds like “increasing.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: To***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Aimed to increasing” is grammatically wrong. “To” would require the base verb (“aimed to increase”), not the gerund “increasing.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: At***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The standard collocation is “aimed at + gerund/noun.” Hence, “aimed at increasing female literacy rates” is the proper construction.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4 (At)**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The verb phrase **“aimed at”** is a fixed collocation in English, used when describing goals directed toward an action or outcome.
 
• Examples: “The policy is aimed at reducing poverty.” / “The campaign is aimed at raising awareness.”
 
• This construction highlights the **purpose or target** of the initiative.

• This is **incorrect**. The structure is awkward and ungrammatical; “to launch initiatives was worked together” is not a valid passive construction.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Initiatives had launched by international organisations and local governments.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The verb form “had launched” is wrong in passive voice; it should be “had been launched” if past perfect passive were intended.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: International organisations and local governments were being worked together to launch initiatives.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The subject changes meaning, and “were being worked together” is grammatically faulty and illogical.
 
 

Therefore, the correct passive transformation is **Option 1**: *“Initiatives were launched together by international organisations and local governments.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In passive voice, the **object** of the active sentence becomes the **subject**.
 
• The verb form changes to include **“be + past participle”**.
 
• The agent (doer) is introduced with **“by”** if necessary.
 
• Active: “International organisations and local governments worked together to launch initiatives.”

 Passive: “Initiatives were launched together by international organisations and local governments.”

subject: ENG
question: Which sentence from the passage is written in the present perfect tense?

options.text: Every hospital employee plays a critical role.
Many remain committed to their work.
Awareness about the importance of every hospital worker has grown.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **Present Perfect Tense**, we look for the specific verb structure: **Has/Have + Past Participle (V3)**.
 
• In **Option 4**, the sentence "Awareness... **has grown**" follows this exact formula (*has* + the third form of the verb *grow*). This tense is used to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or began in the past and continues to the present.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Hospitals **operate**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
• **Option 2:** "...employee **plays**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1 + s).
 
• **Option 3:** "Many **remain**..." is in the **Simple Present Tense** (V1).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, identifying tenses is a foundational skill. Always remember that the Present Perfect ("has grown") links the past to the present, whereas the Simple Past ("grew") would imply the action is finished and disconnected from now.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect:** Subject + has/have + V3 (e.g., has worked, have seen).
 
• **Simple Present:** Subject + V1 (s/es) (e.g., works, see).
 
• **Tireless:** Having or showing great effort or energy.
 
• **Psychological weight:** The mental or emotional burden of a situation.

subject: ENG
question: Which sentence from the passage contains a modal verb?

options.text: Nurses may have to attend to critical patients for entire shifts without rest.
Emergency ward staff often faces life-or-death situations.
The life of a hospital employee is marked by long hours.
Hospital employees witness suffering, grief, and loss.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the sentence with a **Modal Verb**, we look for auxiliary (helping) verbs that express necessity, possibility, permission, or ability. Common modal verbs include *can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will,* and *would*.
 
• In **Option 1**, the word **"may"** is a modal verb used to express **possibility** or a likely scenario. The phrase "may have to" combines this possibility with an obligation.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Emergency ward staff often **faces**..." uses a main verb in the simple present tense. "Often" is an adverb, not a modal verb.
 
• **Option 3:** "...employee **is marked**..." uses a helping verb "is" (part of the passive voice structure), but it is a primary auxiliary, not a modal.
 
• **Option 4:** "Hospital employees **witness**..." uses a simple action verb (V1) without any auxiliary.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, modal verbs are frequently tested because they change the "mood" or "tone" of a sentence. "Nurses attend" (a fact) is very different from "Nurses **may** have to attend" (a potential requirement).*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modal Verb:** A verb that is used with another verb to express ideas such as possibility, permission, or intention.
 
• **Precision:** The quality, condition, or fact of being exact and accurate.
 
• **Compassion:** Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
 
• **Around the clock:** Happening all day and all night.

subject: ENG
question:
"Silver ornaments have been a part of women's jewellery collections for centuries..."

why is the verb "have" used instead of "has"?

options.text: Because the sentence is in passive voice

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This question tests the rule of **Subject-Verb Agreement**.
 
• In the sentence: *"Silver **ornaments have** been a part..."* the noun **"ornaments"** is the head of the subject phrase.
 
• Since **"ornaments"** is a **plural countable noun**, it requires a plural verb (**have**).
 
• If the subject were simply "Silver" (uncountable), we would use "has," but here "Silver" acts as an adjective modifying the plural noun "ornaments."
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** While "silver" is uncountable, it is not the functional subject here; "ornaments" is. If "silver" were the subject, the verb would be the singular "has."
 
• **Option 3:** "Collections" is part of the **object/complement** phrase ("part of... collections"), not the subject. The verb must agree with the subject that comes before it.
 
• **Option 4:** The sentence is in the **Present Perfect Tense** (active voice), not passive voice. "Have been" here indicates a state that started in the past and continues to the present.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, examiners often place a singular noun (like "Silver") right before a plural subject (like "ornaments") to trick you. Always identify the **main noun** that the verb is actually describing.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** The grammatical rule that the verb or verbs in a sentence must match the number, person, and gender of the subject.
 
• **Uncountable Nouns:** Nouns like *water, silver, advice* that cannot be counted and usually take a singular verb.
 
• **Countable Nouns:** Nouns like *ornament, book, chair* that can be pluralized and take plural verbs.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• This is **active voice**. The subject “Gold” performs the action “holds.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Several factors contribute to the rise***
 
 
• This is **active voice**. The subject “Several factors” performs the action “contribute.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: The current hype surrounding gold rates is not entirely based on practical factors***
 
 
• This is **passive voice**. The subject “hype” is described as being “based on” something, showing the action is received rather than performed.
 
 

Therefore, the correct passive voice sentence is **Option 4**: *“The current hype surrounding gold rates is not entirely based on practical factors.”*

• In **active voice**, the subject performs the action (e.g., “Gold holds cultural value”).
 
• In **passive voice**, the subject receives the action (e.g., “is based on practical factors”).
 
• Passive voice often uses forms of “be + past participle.”

subject: ENG
question:
Identify the type of clause in the sentence:

"Once dense forests, which acted as vital carbon sinks and habitats for myriad species, are now alarmingly fragmented."
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the type of clause, we examine the segment: **"...which acted as vital carbon sinks and habitats for myriad species..."**
 
• An **Adjective Clause** (also known as a Relative Clause) is a dependent clause that modifies a noun or pronoun. It usually begins with a relative pronoun like *who, whom, whose, that,* or *which*.
 
• In this sentence, the clause starts with **"which"** and provides additional descriptive information about the noun **"forests."** Since it functions as an adjective by describing the forests, it is an adjective clause.
 
• Specifically, this is a **non-restrictive adjective clause** because it is set off by commas and provides extra information that is not essential to the identity of the noun it modifies.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** An **Adverb clause** modifies a verb, adjective, or adverb. It usually answers questions like *when, where, why,* or *how* (e.g., "Because the forests were cut...").
 
• **Option 3:** A **Noun clause** acts as a noun within the sentence (e.g., "I know *that forests are important*").
 
• **Option 4:** A **Coordinate clause** is one of two or more independent clauses of equal importance in a compound sentence, usually joined by a coordinating conjunction like *and, but,* or *or*.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level grammar sections for exams, identifying clauses is crucial. A quick tip: if a clause starts with "which" or "who" and immediately follows a noun, it is almost certainly an **Adjective Clause**.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon Sink:** A natural environment (like a forest) that absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
 
• **Myriad:** A countless or extremely great number.
 
• **Fragmented:** Broken into small or separate parts; in ecology, this refers to the breaking up of continuous habitats.
 
• **Relative Pronoun:** A word used to connect a relative clause to a noun or pronoun (e.g., which, that, who).

• To identify the type of noun for **"proliferation,"** we must look at its definition and how it is perceived.
 
• **Proliferation** refers to a rapid increase in numbers or a large amount of something (in this context, construction activities).
 
• An **Abstract Noun** represents a concept, quality, or state rather than a concrete object. You cannot touch, see, smell, taste, or hear "proliferation" itself; you can only see the results of it (the buildings).
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** A **Proper noun** is a specific name for a particular person, place, or organization (e.g., Himachal Pradesh). These always start with a capital letter.
 
• **Option 3:** A **Concrete noun** refers to something that can be perceived by the five senses (e.g., timber, water, plastic).
 
• **Option 4:** A **Collective noun** refers to a group of individuals or things taken as a whole (e.g., myriad, species, staff).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, nouns ending in suffixes like **-tion, -ness, -ity, -ism,** and **-ment** are almost always **Abstract Nouns**. They describe an idea or a process rather than a physical item.*

question: In the sentence, “The persistence of such barriers underscores the necessity for institutional reforms aimed at amplifying female representation in executive roles,” the phrase “aimed at amplifying female representation” is:

options.text: an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2) a participial phrase modifying “reforms”***

 
 
• This is the **correct** answer. The phrase begins with the past participle "aimed." It functions as an adjectival phrase directly describing the noun preceding it, "reforms." It tells us specifically what kind of institutional reforms are necessary—those that are aimed at amplifying female representation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (a misplaced modifier)**: Incorrect because it is placed perfectly adjacent to the noun it describes ("reforms"), meaning there is no grammatical ambiguity about what is being modified.
 
• **Option 3 (an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence)**: Incorrect because an absolute phrase typically features a noun or pronoun alongside a participle modifying the whole clause (e.g., "The reforms having passed, the board celebrated"), which doesn't fit the syntax here.
 
• **Option 4 (an infinitive phrase modifying “necessity”)**: Incorrect because an infinitive phrase requires the word "to" followed by the base form of a verb (e.g., "to aim").

• **Option 4 (an immediate reversal)**: Incorrect because "reconfiguration" means rearranging parts into a new form, not necessarily going backward or reversing, and "nuanced" does not relate to the speed (immediacy) of the action.

Complete transparency in government surveillance activities

question: The word "**exacerbates**" in the passage "erratic weather patterns attributed to climate change, further exacerbates the fragile ecosystem's vulnerability." most nearly means:

__
 
• To find the most appropriate meaning of **"exacerbates,"** we look at its context: *"...compounded by erratic weather patterns... further **exacerbates** the fragile ecosystem's vulnerability."*
 
• The passage discusses negative factors like overexploitation and climate change. When a negative situation is "compounded," it means it is being made more intense or severe.
 
• **Exacerbate** means to make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling **worse**. In this sentence, the existing vulnerability of the ecosystem is being increased or worsened by the weather patterns.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** **Alleviates** means to make suffering or a problem **less severe**. This is an antonym.
 
• **Option 3:** **Mitigates** means to make something less severe, serious, or painful. This is also an antonym.
 
• **Option 4:** **Initiates** means to cause a process or action to **begin**. While these factors might start new problems, "exacerbate" specifically refers to making an existing condition worse.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, "Contextual Vocabulary" often involves identifying synonyms and antonyms within the same question. Options 1 and 3 are synonyms of each other (meaning 'to reduce'), which often signals that they are both incorrect if only one answer is allowed.*

• **Burgeoning:** Beginning to grow or increase rapidly; flourishing.

question: Identify the voice in "Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare".
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Identification of the Voice:***

 
 
• The phrase uses the past participle **"conceived."** In the full context of the sentence, it implies that "Chaturanga was initially conceived..."
 
• In **Passive Voice**, the subject of the sentence (Chaturanga) is the receiver of the action, not the doer. The game did not "conceive" itself; it was conceived by people/creators.
 
 
 
• ***Structural Analysis:***
 
 
• **Active Voice equivalent**: "Creators initially conceived Chaturanga as a strategic simulation..." (The subject performs the action).
 
• **Passive Voice (this phrase)**: "Initially conceived..." (The focus is on the thing being created/conceived).
 
 
 
• ***Analysis of Other Options:***
 
 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the subject is not performing the action of conceiving.
 
• **Option 3**: **Middle Voice** is a grammatical voice where the subject both performs and is affected by the action (e.g., "The door opened"). This does not apply here.
 
• **Option 4**: **Causative Voice** indicates that the subject causes someone else to do something (e.g., "I had my hair cut"). This is not present in the phrase.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Passive voice.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Utility**: Authors often use passive voice when the actor (the person who conceived the game) is unknown, irrelevant, or less important than the object (the game itself).
 
• **Past Participle as Adjective**: In this specific phrase, "conceived" acts as a participle modifying "chaturanga," but its underlying grammatical relationship to the noun remains passive.

• The original sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** ("play"). 
 
• The formula for Passive Voice in Simple Present is: **New Subject + am/is/are + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object**. 
 
 
• **Active Subject:** Parents and schools
 
• **Active Verb:** play
 
• **Active Object:** A pivotal role
 
• **Passive Transformation:** "A pivotal role" (New Subject) + "is" (Auxiliary) + "played" (V3) + "by parents and schools" (New Object).
 
 
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** The meaning is reversed, suggesting the parents are being played by the role.
 
• **Option 3:** This uses **"was,"** which changes the tense to Simple Past. The tense must remain consistent.
 
• **Option 4:** This uses **"play"** (V1) instead of the required Past Participle **"played"** (V3).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, voice change questions often try to trick you by changing the tense. Always identify the tense of the main verb first; if the active is present, the passive must use "is/am/are."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pivotal:** Central and important to the situation.
 
• **Lifestyle diseases:** Diseases linked with the way people live (e.g., Type 2 diabetes, heart disease).
 
• **Nourishment:** The food or other substances necessary for growth and health.
 
• **Adolescents:** Young people in the process of developing from a child into an adult.

• The question requires converting a sentence with two clauses from Active Voice to Passive Voice.
 
• Active Voice: Families (Subject) can enjoy (Verb) technology (Object) while safeguarding (Verb) their youngest members (Object).
 
• In the first clause, "technology" becomes the subject, and "can enjoy" becomes **"can be enjoyed."**
 
• In the second clause, "youngest members" becomes the subject, and the participle "safeguarding" is converted to the passive form **"are safeguarded."**
 
• **Option 1** correctly transforms both parts of the sentence while maintaining the original meaning and tense (present/modal capability).

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

 

**Grammar Insight:** *When converting a sentence with a modal verb like "can," the passive structure is **Subject + modal + be + Past Participle (V3)**. Similarly, the continuous/participle action "safeguarding" must be reflected as a state in the passive voice to indicate that the protection is being provided to the members.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

In the following sentence, identify the finite verb(s):

"The pandemic further **aggravated **these conditions by **transitioning **most work to virtual platforms, **blurring **the boundaries between professional and personal life, and **extending **working hours indefinitely."

The correct answer is **Option 1**.

__
 
• **Finite Verb Definition:** A finite verb is a verb that has a specific subject and shows **tense** (past, present, or future) and **number** (singular or plural). It acts as the main verb of a clause.
 
• **Analysis of "Aggravated":** In the sentence, **"aggravated"** is the finite verb because it is the main action performed by the subject ("The pandemic") and is in the **simple past tense**.
 
• **Non-Finite Verbs:** The words **transitioning**, **blurring**, and **extending** are present participles (gerunds/participles acting as objects of the preposition "by"). They do not show tense on their own and do not have a direct subject-verb agreement in this structure, making them **non-finite**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Identifying Finite Verbs:** You can identify a finite verb by checking if it changes when you change the tense (e.g., *"The pandemic **aggravates**..."*) or the subject number.
 
• **Contextual Vocabulary:** The word **"aggravated"** in the passage means to make a problem or injury worse or more serious.
 
• **Sentence Structure:** The subject is **"The pandemic,"** the finite verb is **"aggravated,"** and the rest of the sentence provides additional information through participial phrases.

__
 
• ***Understanding the Interrogative Negative.***

 
 
• An **Interrogative Negative** sentence is a question that also contains a negation (not). It is often used to confirm a fact that the speaker believes to be true or to express surprise.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** ("India imposes..."). To form a question in this tense, we use the auxiliary verb **do** or **does**. Since "India" is a singular subject, we use **does**.
 
 
 
• ***Structure of the Transformation.***
 
 
• The standard formula for an interrogative negative sentence is: **Auxiliary Verb + Subject + Not + Main Verb...?** or the contracted form: **Auxiliary Verb-n't + Subject + Main Verb...?**
 
• Original: *India imposes...*
 
• Interrogative Negative: ***Doesn't** India **impose**...?* (Note that when using 'does', the main verb 'imposes' loses its '-s' and returns to its base form 'impose').
 
 
 
• ***Evaluating the Options.***
 
 
• **Option 1**: This is a simple Interrogative sentence (positive question), not negative.
 
• **Option 2**: This is a 'Wh-' question and is grammatically incorrect (missing the auxiliary 'does').
 
• **Option 4**: This is in the **Past Tense** ("Did"), whereas the original sentence is in the Present Tense.
